correctness.rationale: For each r>=4, the cyclic (r+1)-uniform morphism a->a^r(a+1 mod3) generates all nine letter-adjacency pairs, so every length-(r+1)^m factor can be placed in a concatenation of two level-m blocks. The weighted maximal factor has a general upper bound r*max_a W_m(a)+H_m; the nesting of a maximizer and the two possible ordered block boundaries gives equality for all real letter weights, hence the exact recurrence for the number of zero-count values. The letter-count vector evolves by rI+C; the cyclotomic eigenangle is irrational modulo pi because its twice-cosine is rational but a noninteger algebraic integer were it rational. Modulo two, at m=3t a unique exceptional letter parity makes the range gap even precisely when the irrational rotation visits a fixed proper arc, a nonperiodic word. A k-regular sequence modulo a fixed positive integer is k-automatic, and a k-automatic sequence evaluated at k^m is eventually periodic, contradicting this parity subsequence. Independent enumerations verify the finite base cases only.

originality.rationale: The closest Allouche et al. 2026 paper proves a 2-automatic/4-automatic nonregular abelian-complexity example at the fixed repetition count r=3, and the present theorem treats all r>=4 via a new uniform induction and parity reduction.
